exercise_phases.name: Setup
cues: Head, upper back and glutes on the bench, both feet flat on the floor
Shoulder blades pulled back and down
Closed, pronated grip, hands evenly spaced

exercise_phases.name: Unrack
cues: Lift the bar off the rests with straight arms
Bring it over the shoulders without losing the shoulder position

exercise_phases.name: Starting position
cues: Arms straight, bar over the shoulder joints

exercise_phases.name: Eccentric (lowering)
cues: Lower the bar under control to the lower chest
Elbows travel down and slightly towards the body, not straight out to the sides

exercise_phases.name: Bottom position
cues: Bar touches the chest lightly, no bounce
Glutes and shoulders stay on the bench

exercise_phases.name: Concentric (pressing)
cues: Press the bar up and back towards the shoulders
Keep the wrists straight and the feet planted

exercise_phases.name: Lockout
cues: Elbows fully extended, bar over the shoulders

exercise_phases.name: Finish (re-rack)
cues: Move the bar back to the uprights with straight arms
Lower it into the rests under control

loop_segment.comment: One repetition that starts and ends in the same pose; used for looping clips.

movement.grip_note: Grip: 0.78 m between hand centres (technique.grip_width_between_hand_centres_m). PRIMARY BASIS per the owner correction of 14/11/2026: comparison against the people in licensed reference clips — the same absolute grip as real lifters (0.74 m in the Wikimedia Commons / FitnessScape clip, 0.79 m in the YMove clip, each +/-0.04-0.06 m; see reference_measurements_medium_grip.json and REFERENCE_EVAL_2026-11-14.md, PR #893). The grip/shoulder-width ratio of the clip lifters could NOT be measured reliably from the available clips (shoulder joint centres occluded and foreshortened in the front view; two independent methods disagreed by 0.08 m), so no clip-grounded ratio is claimed. SECONDARY REFERENCE ONLY: on Mausehund et al. 2022's relative scale the 0.78 m grip reads wide (214% of the character's 0.358 m shoulder-joint distance, a joint-centre proxy for biacromial distance — approximate), while the bottom kinematics follow the study's medium-condition pattern (flexion 105.8 deg vs medium 101.4, abduction 50.1 deg vs medium 59.3). Study samples differ in proportions from the clip lifters, so study scales are corroboration only, never the primary basis. DECISION (a), 14/11/2026: Kiet delegated the grip call to C; C accepted the wide-relative grip + deep bottom + tucked elbows as the standard barbell bench press guide, because the motion matches real lifting and narrowing to ~0.58 m would make the guide less like real lifting. The 'medium grip' label formerly implied by the brief is corrected by this note. Known limitation accepted by the owner 14/11/2026: elbows below the pad at the bottom (character-003 geometry; see BOTTOM_POSE_FINDINGS.md, PR #891).

technique.comment: Parameters of this demonstration (approved 14/11/2026; see approval_basis). Each one cites reference_notes.json; none is a universal 'correct' value and reasonable lifters differ in all of them.

placement.comment: Where the lifter lies on the bench: distance from the head end of the pad to the top of the head.

validation_profile.comment: Thresholds for automated checks. They catch defects in the animation data (jumps, slides, penetration, asymmetry). They do not certify exercise technique; technique approval is recorded separately (status, reviewer, approval_date, approval_basis).
validation_profile.max_hand_into_bar_comment: The skin of the palm is rigid in this rig. Up to 8 mm of palm pad inside the bar stands for soft tissue pressed flat by the load; more than that, or any finger passing through the bar, is a defect.

technical_cues: Five points of contact: head, upper back and glutes on the bench, both feet on the floor
Grip the bar evenly with a closed grip, wider than shoulder width
Lower the bar under control to the lower chest
Keep the forearms vertical and the wrists over the elbows
Press until the elbows are extended, with the bar over the shoulders
common_mistakes: Bouncing the bar off the chest
Lifting the glutes off the bench
Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides
Uneven grip or one side of the bar leading
Feet moving or lifting during the repetition
reviewer: C (Muse) — reference-comparison approval per owner decision 14/11/2026 + delegated grip decision (a) (no expert review; no budget)
approval_basis: Reference-clip evaluation 2026-11-14 (PR #893, docs/exercise-visual-system/REFERENCE_EVAL_2026-11-14.md): grip 0.78 m matches licensed reference clips (0.74 m Commons/FitnessScape, 0.79 m YMove); bottom elbow flexion 105.8 deg, forearms vertical (5.0 deg from vertical), bar touches the chest, controlled 2 s / 2 s tempo — the motion matches real lifting and standard coaching. Grip/kinematics tension against Mausehund's relative scale resolved by delegated decision (a) 14/11/2026 (Kiet delegated the call to C; see grip_note): the wide-relative grip + deep bottom + tucked elbows is accepted as the standard barbell bench press guide. The clip lifters' grip/shoulder ratio could not be measured reliably and is not claimed. Basis is comparison against real movement per the owner decisions of 14/11/2026, NOT expert review (no budget). Known limitation accepted by the owner 14/11/2026: elbows below the pad at the bottom (character-003 geometry; BOTTOM_POSE_FINDINGS.md section 7, PR #891). Caveats: bench clip elbow angles from MediaPipe were unreliable (occlusion) — the elbow comparison rests on published data + bone measurement; motion smoothness was judged from stills only; the USDZ shipped in the app is the evaluated character-003 export (63 bones, 105.79 deg — verified by reimport), replacing the old 53-bone / 136 deg file.
muscle_roles_note: Pectoralis major, anterior deltoid and triceps brachii are the agonists in the systematic review by Stastny et al. 2017 (reference_notes.json). Stabilisers are listed from the same review's discussion, where the evidence is thinner; they are recorded here but not highlighted in the render (highlight_roles).
